metadata.title: Fast Mixing in Sparse Random Ising Models

extraction_notes.note: Environment is a 'Definition' labelled lem:poincare whose body states the Poincare inequality; kept as definition of the Poincare constant rather than lemma since it fixes what PI(nu) means.
Remark that only introduces the names 'bulk' and 'near-forest part'; retyped as definition.

The technical overview states informal versions of later theorems and definitions, and describes an informal exploration process in an enumerate list; kept as separate nodes (content differs) linked to the formal versions by mention edges, and the process as an unmarked algorithm.
Many results are restated through thmtools restatable macros (e.g. \spinglassmixing*), so proofs following a restatement are not syntactically attached; proves edges were added by reading.

The proof of thm:centered-adjacency begins in running text (reduction to covariance bounds of J_R) and finishes in a proof environment after an informal plan; emitted as two proof parts with a continuation edge.
Survey statements in the introduction (worst-case sampling conditions, stochastic-localization literature) and heuristic branching-process discussion in the overview were left as text, not nodes.

The proof-sketch rule asks for rigor: semi_formal on a sketch proof node, while the rigor rule (and the finishing step) says rigor never goes on proofs; kept semi_formal per the sketch rule, leaving one finishing-step warning.

nodes.name: Ising model (Gibbs distribution with inverse temperature)
nodes.statement: These are probability distributions of the form \begin{align*} \mu_{\beta}(\sigma) = \mu_{\beta J,h}(\sigma) \propto \exp\parens*{\frac{\beta}{2}\sigma^{\top} J \sigma + \langle h,\sigma\rangle}, \qquad \forall \sigma \in \{\pm1\}^{n}, \end{align*} where $J \in \R^{n \times n}$ is a symmetric \emph{interaction matrix}, $h \in \R^{n}$ is an \emph{external field} vector, and $\beta \geq 0$ is the \emph{inverse temperature}, which scales the interaction strengths.
nodes.statement_short: The Ising Gibbs measure $\mu_\beta(\sigma)\propto\exp(\frac{\beta}{2}\sigma^\top J\sigma+\langle h,\sigma\rangle)$ on $\{\pm1\}^n$.

nodes.name: Tractability of sampling from Ising models
nodes.statement: Under what conditions on $\beta$, $J$, and $h$ is (approximately) sampling from $\mu_{\beta}$ computationally tractable?
nodes.statement_short: For which $\beta$, $J$, $h$ is approximate sampling from the Ising model tractable?

nodes.name: Spectral condition for rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics
nodes.statement: A recent line of work \cite{BB19, EKZ22, CE22, KLR22, BBD23, AJKPV24} has identified that having spectral diameter bounded as \begin{align} \text{(Spectral Condition)} \qquad \beta \cdot \parens*{\lambda_{\max}(J) - \lambda_{\min}(J)} < 1 \end{align} is sufficient to ensure that Glauber dynamics mixes in $O(n\log n)$ steps.
nodes.origin_citation: BB19; EKZ22; CE22; KLR22; BBD23; AJKPV24
assumptions: \beta \cdot \parens*{\lambda_{\max}(J) - \lambda_{\min}(J)} < 1
conclusions: Glauber dynamics mixes in $O(n\log n)$ steps
nodes.statement_short: Spectral diameter of $\beta J$ below 1 implies $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics.

nodes.name: Spectral Condition
nodes.statement: \text{(Spectral Condition)} \qquad \beta \cdot \parens*{\lambda_{\max}(J) - \lambda_{\min}(J)} < 1
nodes.origin_citation: BB19; EKZ22; CE22; KLR22; BBD23; AJKPV24
nodes.label: eq:spectral-condition

nodes.name: Fast mixing for the Viana--Bray diluted spin glass
nodes.statement: Fix a constant $d > 1$. There exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that for all $\beta \leq C/\sqrt{d}$ the following is true. Let $A$ be the random matrix such that each off-diagonal entry is equal to $0$ with probability $1-d/n$, and is equally likely to be $\pm 1$ with the remaining probability. With high probability over the draw of $A$, Glauber dynamics run on $\mu_{\beta A}$ mixes in time $n^{1+o_n(1)}$.
assumptions: Fix a constant $d > 1$.
for all $\beta \leq C/\sqrt{d}$
Let $A$ be the random matrix such that each off-diagonal entry is equal to $0$ with probability $1-d/n$, and is equally likely to be $\pm 1$ with the remaining probability.
conclusions: With high probability over the draw of $A$, Glauber dynamics run on $\mu_{\beta A}$ mixes in time $n^{1+o_n(1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $\beta\le C/\sqrt d$, Glauber dynamics on a randomly signed sparse Erdos-Renyi Ising model mixes in $n^{1+o(1)}$ time whp.
nodes.label: th:main

nodes.name: Polynomial mixing threshold $d\tanh^2(\beta)<1$ for Viana--Bray
nodes.statement: Based on replica-symmetry breaking predictions from statistical physics, e.g., \cite{GT04}, we further conjecture that Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time if $d \tanh^2(\beta)<1$, and takes exponential time to mix above this threshold.
assumptions: $d \tanh^2(\beta)<1$
conclusions: Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time
takes exponential time to mix above this threshold

takes exponential time to mix above this threshold

nodes.statement_short: Glauber dynamics for the diluted spin glass mixes polynomially iff $d\tanh^2\beta<1$.

nodes.name: Extension to slightly super-constant degree
nodes.statement: We further believe that our methods extend to the regime where $d$ is slightly super-constant, in particular when $d < \log n$. In the setting where $d > \log n$, the spectral condition (\Cref{eq:spectral-condition}) can be used to bound the mixing time for $\beta = O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\right)$.

nodes.name: Community signal vector
nodes.statement: Let $\bsigma \in \{\pm1\}^{n}$ be a \emph{signal} vector drawn uniformly at random, which intuitively encodes the ground truth community assignments.

nodes.name: Stochastic block model graph generation
nodes.statement: Given $\bsigma$, we draw a random graph $\bG$ by including an edge between $u,v \in [n]$ independently with probability $\frac{d + \lambda \sqrt{d}}{n}$ if $\bsigma(u) = \bsigma(v)$, and with probability $\frac{d - \lambda\sqrt{d}}{n}$ otherwise, where $d, \lambda \in \R$ are fixed constants.
nodes.statement_short: Edges appear independently with probability $(d\pm\lambda\sqrt d)/n$ depending on whether endpoints share a community.

nodes.name: Stochastic block model $\SBM(n,d,\lambda)$
nodes.statement: The entirety of this generative process induces a distribution over graphs denoted $\SBM(n, d, \lambda)$, with the special case $\lambda = 0$ recovering the Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi graph $\ER(n,d/n)$.

nodes.name: Fast mixing for Ising models on centered SBM adjacency matrices
nodes.statement: Fix constants $d > 1, \lambda \geq 0$. There exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that for all $\beta \leq C/\sqrt{d}$ the following is true. Let $\ol{A}_{\bG} \coloneqq A_{\bG} - \E[A_{\bG}|\bsigma]$ be the centered adjacency matrix of $\bG \sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$. With high probability over the draw of $\bG$, Glauber dynamics run on $\mu_{\beta\ol{A}_{\bG}}$ mixes in time $n^{1+o_d(1)}$.
assumptions: Fix constants $d > 1, \lambda \geq 0$.
for all $\beta \leq C/\sqrt{d}$
Let $\ol{A}_{\bG} \coloneqq A_{\bG} - \E[A_{\bG}|\bsigma]$ be the centered adjacency matrix of $\bG \sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$.
conclusions: With high probability over the draw of $\bG$, Glauber dynamics run on $\mu_{\beta\ol{A}_{\bG}}$ mixes in time $n^{1+o_d(1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $\beta\le C/\sqrt d$, Glauber dynamics for the Ising model with centered SBM adjacency interactions mixes in $n^{1+o(1)}$ time whp.
nodes.label: thm:main-centered

nodes.name: Mossel--Sly mixing for ferromagnetic Ising on sparse random graphs
nodes.statement: In the ferromagnetic case where $J = A_{\bG}$, Mossel \& Sly \cite{ms13} established a mixing time of $n^{1 + \Theta(1/\log\log n)}$ for Glauber dynamics in the regime $d \tanh(\beta) < 1$ with high probability over $\bG \sim \ER(n,d/n)$.
assumptions: $d \tanh(\beta) < 1$
conclusions: a mixing time of $n^{1 + \Theta(1/\log\log n)}$ for Glauber dynamics

nodes.name: Efthymiou--Zampetakis almost-quadratic mixing
nodes.statement: More recently, when $J$ is supported on $\bG \sim \ER(n,d/n)$ and has i.i.d. Gaussian entries, Efthymiou \& Zampetakis \cite{EZ24} established almost-quadratic mixing of Glauber dynamics when $\beta \leq \sqrt{2\pi}/d$, and conjectured that their regime of $\beta$ is optimal for rapid mixing.
assumptions: $J$ is supported on $\bG \sim \ER(n,d/n)$ and has i.i.d. Gaussian entries
$\beta \leq \sqrt{2\pi}/d$

nodes.name: Bauerschmidt--Bodineau--Dagallier Kawasaki dynamics mixing
nodes.statement: In a recent work, Bauerschmidt, Bodineau \& Dagallier \cite{BBD23} proved that the Kawasaki dynamics for the ferromagnetic Ising model with fixed magnetisation on a random $d$-regular graph mixes rapidly for $\beta < O\left(1/\sqrt{d}\right)$.
assumptions: ferromagnetic Ising model with fixed magnetisation on a random $d$-regular graph
$\beta < O\left(1/\sqrt{d}\right)$
conclusions: the Kawasaki dynamics for the ferromagnetic Ising model with fixed magnetisation on a random $d$-regular graph mixes rapidly

nodes.name: Local entropy
nodes.statement: The \emph{local entropy} of $f$ is $\calE_{\mu}\parens*{f, \log f} \coloneqq \E_{\bx,\by}\bracks*{ (f(\bx) - f(\by)) \cdot \log\frac{f(\bx)}{f(\by)} }$ where $\bx\sim\mu$ and $\by$ is sampled by taking a single step of the Glauber dynamics chain from $\bx$.
nodes.statement_short: Local entropy $\calE_\mu(f,\log f)$: expected $(f(x)-f(y))\log(f(x)/f(y))$ over one Glauber step.

nodes.name: Global entropy
nodes.statement: The \emph{global entropy} of $f$ is $\Ent_{\mu}[f]\coloneqq \E_{\mu} f\log f - \E_{\mu} f \log \E_{\mu} f$.

nodes.name: Modified log-Sobolev inequality (informal)
nodes.statement: We say that Glauber dynamics for $\mu$ satisfies a \emph{modified log-Sobolev inequality} (MLSI) if for any function $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\R_{>0}$: \[ \calE_{\mu}(f,\log f) \gtrsim \Ent_{\mu}[f], \] where the $\gtrsim$ hides a $\poly(n)$ factor.
nodes.statement_short: MLSI: local entropy dominates global entropy up to a $\poly(n)$ factor.

nodes.name: MLSI for sparse randomly signed Ising models (informal)
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a randomly signed graph $\bG\sim \ER(n,d/n)$. There exists a constant $\beta = \Omega(1 / \sqrt{d})$ such that $\mu = \mu_{\beta A}$ satisfies an MLSI.
assumptions: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a randomly signed graph $\bG\sim \ER(n,d/n)$.
conclusions: There exists a constant $\beta = \Omega(1 / \sqrt{d})$ such that $\mu = \mu_{\beta A}$ satisfies an MLSI.
nodes.label: thm:MLSI-sparse-ising

nodes.name: Polynomial factor in the MLSI
nodes.statement: In fact, we show that the polynomial factor hidden by $\gtrsim$ in the above is $n^{-1-o(1)}$. However, we do not stress this in the overview for the sake of simplicity.

nodes.name: Conservation of local entropy under mixtures
nodes.statement: The first inequality is generic and does not use any properties of the structure of $\rho$; see, e.g., \cite[Page 19]{AJKPV21a}.
conclusions: The first inequality is generic and does not use any properties of the structure of $\rho$

nodes.name: Proof of conservation of local entropy
nodes.statement: We reproduce the details here for completeness: \begin{align*} \calE_{\mu}(f, \log f) &= \sum_{x\sim y} \frac{1}{n} \cdot \frac{\mu(x) \mu(y)}{\mu(x)+\mu(y)}\cdot\parens*{f(x)-f(y)}\cdot\log\frac{f(x)}{f(y)} \\ &= \sum_{x\sim y} \frac{1}{n} \cdot \frac{\E_{\bz\sim\rho}\left[\mu_{\bz}(x)\right]\cdot \E_{\bz\sim\rho}\left[\mu_{\bz}(y)\right]}{\E_{\bz\sim\rho}\left[\mu_{\bz}(x)\right]+\E_{\bz\sim\rho}\left[\mu_{\bz}(y)\right]}\cdot\parens*{f(x)-f(y)}\cdot\log\frac{f(x)}{f(y)} \\ &\ge \sum_{x\sim y} \frac{1}{n} \cdot \E_{\bz\sim\rho}\left[\frac{\mu_{\bz}(x) \mu_{\bz}(y)}{\mu_{\bz}(x)+\mu_{\bz}(y)}\right]\cdot\parens*{f(x)-f(y)}\cdot\log\frac{f(x)}{f(y)} \\ &= \E_{\bz\sim\rho} \left[\calE_{\mu_{\bz}}(f, \log f)\right], \end{align*} where the inequality follows from concavity of the function $(a,b)\mapsto\frac{ab}{a+b}$ in the nonnegative quadrant.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the Dirichlet form and apply concavity of $(a,b)\mapsto ab/(a+b)$ (Jensen).

nodes.name: Control matrix and Gaussian-smoothed variable
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a PSD matrix that we shall call a \emph{control matrix}, let $\bx\sim\mu$, and let $\bz \coloneqq \bx + M^{-1/2}\bg$ for $\bg\sim\calN(0, I)$ independent of $\bx$.
nodes.statement_short: Control matrix $M$ (PSD); $z=x+M^{-1/2}g$ with Gaussian $g$.

nodes.name: Mixture measure $\rho$ and components $\mu_{\bz}$
nodes.statement: Let $\rho$ denote the distribution of $\bz$ and let $\mu_{\bz}$ denote the distribution of $\bx|\bz$.

nodes.name: Computation of the conditional law of $\bx$ given $\bz$
nodes.statement: Let $P(x), P(z|x)$ and $P(x,z)$ be the joint densities of $\bx$, $\bz|\bx$ and $(\bx,\bz)$ respectively. We have: \begin{align*} \Pr[\bx = x|\bz = z] &\propto P(x, z) \\ &= P(x)\cdot P(z|x) \\ &\propto \exp\parens*{\frac{1}{2}x^{\top}Jx + \angles*{h,x}}\cdot\exp\parens*{-\frac{1}{2}(z-x)^{\top}M(z-x)} \\ &\propto \exp\parens*{\frac{1}{2}x^{\top}(J-M)x + \angles*{h+Mz, x}}\mper \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bayes' rule and completing the square in the Gaussian kernel.

nodes.name: Components of the decomposition are Ising models with interaction $J-M$
nodes.statement: The upshot of the above is that the measures $\mu_{\bz}$ are Ising models with interaction matrix $J-M$ and some external field depending on $\bz$.
conclusions: the measures $\mu_{\bz}$ are Ising models with interaction matrix $J-M$ and some external field depending on $\bz$

nodes.name: Conservation of entropy
nodes.statement: Recall that \emph{conservation of entropy} for our decomposition refers to the following functional inequality. For $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\R_{>0}$: \[ \E_{\bz\sim\rho} \Ent_{\mu_{\bz}}[f] \gtrsim \Ent_{\mu}[f]\mper \]
nodes.statement_short: Conservation of entropy: averaged component entropy dominates global entropy up to poly factors.

nodes.name: Stochastic localization path with entropy derivative bound
nodes.statement: Concretely, there is a stochastic process $(\mu_t)_{0\le t\le 1}$ on the space of probability distributions called \emph{stochastic localization} with the following properties; see \cite[Proposition 39 and Lemma 40]{CE22}:\footnote{We refer the reader to \cite{EAM22} for a nice exposition on stochastic localization and why it indeed charts such a path.} \begin{itemize} \item $\mu_0 = \mu$ and $\mu_1 = \mu_{\bz}$ for $\bz\sim\rho$. \item The function $F(t) = \E \Ent_{\mu_t}[f]$, where the expectation is taken over the randomness in the choice of $\mu_{t}$, satisfies the following lower bound on its derivative: \[ \restr{\frac{\dif F}{\dif t}}{t} \ge -\sup_{h}\norm*{M^{1/2}\cdot\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J-tM,h}}\cdot M^{1/2}}_{\mathrm{op}} \cdot F(t)\mper \numberthis \] \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Stochastic localization interpolates $\mu_0=\mu$ to $\mu_1=\mu_z$ with $F'(t)\ge-\sup_h\|M^{1/2}\Cov(\mu_{J-tM,h})M^{1/2}\|F(t)$.

nodes.name: Entropy conservation from a uniform covariance bound
nodes.statement: If we can show for any $h \in \R^{n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$ that $\norm*{M^{1/2}\cdot\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J-tM, h}}\cdot M^{1/2}}_{\mathrm{op}}\le q$ for some $q > 0$, then \[ F(1) \ge F(0)\cdot\exp\parens*{-q}\mcom \] which, in more familiar terms, is \[ \E_{\bz\sim\rho} \Ent_{\mu_{\bz}}[f] \ge \exp\parens*{-q} \Ent_{\mu}[f]\mper \]
assumptions: for any $h \in \R^{n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$ that $\norm*{M^{1/2}\cdot\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J-tM, h}}\cdot M^{1/2}}_{\mathrm{op}}\le q$ for some $q > 0$

nodes.name: Heuristic: covariance blow-up near high-degree vertices
nodes.statement: Under this pretense, via standard formulas for correlations in tree graphical models, \[ \Cov\parens*{\mu_{J,0}}_{i,j}\approx\Omega\parens*{\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}}^{\mathrm{dist}(i,j)}\mper \] Let $n_{\ell}(i)$ denote the number of neighbors of vertex $i$ at distance exactly $\ell$ from $i$. The entries of the $i$th row corresponding to the distance-$\ell$ neighbors of a vertex $i$ are at least $\parens*{1/d}^{\ell/2}$, and since the operator norm of a matrix is at least the $\ell_2$ norm of any row, we have: \[ \norm*{\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J,0}}}_{\mathrm{op}} \gtrsim \Omega\parens*{\sqrt{\frac{n_{\ell}(i)}{d^{\ell}}}}\mper \] This can be huge if vertex $i$ is abnormally high-degree, or more generally, if vertex $i$ has an abnormally large $\ell$-neighborhood.
nodes.statement_short: On trees, covariances decay like $d^{-\mathrm{dist}/2}$, so large $\ell$-neighborhoods blow up the covariance norm.

nodes.name: Heaviness radius $\ell(v)$ (overview)
nodes.statement: For each vertex $v$, define $\ell(v)$ as the smallest value of $\ell$ such that for all $L\ge \ell$, the number of vertices at distance $\le L$ from $v$ is at most $(d(1+\eps))^L$.

nodes.name: Near-forest $H$ as union of balls (overview)
nodes.statement: Set $H$ as $\bigcup_{v\in V} B_{\ell(v)}(v)$, where $B_{\ell(v)}(v)$ is the radius $\ell(v)$ ball around $v$.

nodes.name: Bulk and near-forest (overview)
nodes.statement: The above gives a natural partition of the graph $G$ into $B \coloneqq G\setminus H$, which we call the \emph{bulk}, and $H$, which we call the \emph{near-forest}.

nodes.name: Graph decomposition lemma (overview)
nodes.statement: For $\bG\sim \ER(n,d/n)$ and random signing $\bc$ of the edges of $\bG$, there exists with high probability a subgraph $H$ and $\eps = O(\log d / d)^{1/3}$ such that: \begin{itemize} \item Every connected component of $H$ is a tree plus at most one additional edge. \item The diameter of each connected component of $H$ is at most $O\parens*{\frac{\log n}{\eps^3 d}}$. \item For any vertex $v$ and $\ell \ge 1$, the size of $B_{\ell}(v)$ is at most $\Delta \cdot \parens*{d(1+\eps)}^{\ell-1}$ for $\Delta = o(\log n)$. \item For any vertex $v$ and $\ell \ge 1$, the size of $B_{\ell}(v) \cap B$ is at most $(d(1+\eps))^{\ell}$ where $B$ is the set of all vertices touched by an edge in $\bG\setminus H$. \item The spectral radius of the signed adjacency matrix of $\bG\setminus H$ is at most $2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps)$. \end{itemize}
assumptions: For $\bG\sim \ER(n,d/n)$ and random signing $\bc$ of the edges of $\bG$
conclusions: there exists with high probability a subgraph $H$ and $\eps = O(\log d / d)^{1/3}$ such that
nodes.statement_short: Whp $\ER(n,d/n)$ splits into a near-forest $H$ of small diameter and growth plus a bulk with spectral radius $\le 2\sqrt d(1+\eps)$.
nodes.label: lem:graph-decomp-overview

nodes.name: Control matrix choice for the spin glass
nodes.statement: The above statement motivates the choice of the control matrix as: \[ M\coloneqq\beta\cdot\parens*{ A_{\bG \setminus H} + 2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps)\cdot I_{\bG\setminus H}}\mper \]

nodes.name: Covariance formula for tree Ising models
nodes.statement: There is a simple explicit formula for the covariance matrix of an Ising model on a tree with zero external field in terms of the interaction matrix: for a pair of vertices $i$ and $j$, and the unique path $P$ between $i$ and $j$, the covariance $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{F,0}}_{i,j}$ is equal to $\prod_{e\in P}\tanh(J_e)$.
assumptions: an Ising model on a tree with zero external field
for a pair of vertices $i$ and $j$, and the unique path $P$ between $i$ and $j$
conclusions: the covariance $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{F,0}}_{i,j}$ is equal to $\prod_{e\in P}\tanh(J_e)$

nodes.name: $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandomness (informal)
nodes.statement: We say a graph $H$ is \emph{$(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom} if for every vertex $v\in V(H)$, the number of vertices at distance at most $\ell$ from $v$ is at most $\Delta\cdot D^{\ell-1}$.

nodes.name: MLSI for pseudorandom tree Ising models (informal)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\Delta = o(\log n)$ and $0\le \gamma < 1$ is an absolute constant. Then, for any $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom tree $H$ with interaction matrix $J$ with all entries in $\parens*{-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}, \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}}$ and any external field $h$, Glauber dynamics for $\mu_{J,h}$ satisfies an MLSI.
assumptions: Suppose $\Delta = o(\log n)$ and $0\le \gamma < 1$ is an absolute constant.
for any $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom tree $H$ with interaction matrix $J$ with all entries in $\parens*{-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}, \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}}$ and any external field $h$
conclusions: Glauber dynamics for $\mu_{J,h}$ satisfies an MLSI.

nodes.name: Proof sketch that the excision is a near-forest
nodes.statement: In fact, the above lemma can be used to rule out the existence of multiple cycles in any connected set of vertices (in particular the components of $H$), as long as the diameter of this set is $O(\log n)$. The idea is to rule out the existence of the second cycle by considering the small set of vertices consisting of the two cycles, along with the shortest path between them. Because of the diameter bound, the total size of this set is also $O(\log n)$, so the above lemma applies --- if the hidden constant in the diameter bound is small enough, then the lemma implies that this subgraph has at most one cycle, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Two cycles plus a shortest path between them form a small connected set with tree-excess 2, contradicting the small-set lemma.

nodes.name: Reduce to the diameter bound
nodes.statement: In fact, the above lemma can be used to rule out the existence of multiple cycles in any connected set of vertices (in particular the components of $H$), as long as the diameter of this set is $O(\log n)$.
nodes.statement_short: The small-set lemma rules out two cycles in components of logarithmic diameter.

nodes.name: Two cycles and a shortest path
nodes.statement: The idea is to rule out the existence of the second cycle by considering the small set of vertices consisting of the two cycles, along with the shortest path between them.
nodes.statement_short: Consider the set formed by two cycles and the path between them.

nodes.name: Contradiction via small-set lemma
nodes.statement: Because of the diameter bound, the total size of this set is also $O(\log n)$, so the above lemma applies --- if the hidden constant in the diameter bound is small enough, then the lemma implies that this subgraph has at most one cycle, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: This set is small, so it has at most one cycle: contradiction.

nodes.name: Exploration process generating the near-forest
nodes.statement: Consider the following exploration process, which simulates the ball-growing process that generates $H$. At all stages of the exploration, we maintain a set of active vertices, unexplored vertices, and inactive vertices. The active vertices represent the boundary of the connected component we are currently exploring. \begin{enumerate} \item If there are no active vertices, select a vertex $v$ which has not been explored yet. If all vertices have been visited, terminate the process. \item Select a vertex $v$ in the active set, and iteratively query its radius-$r$ neighborhoods. \item If there is some vertex $u$ at distance at most $r$ which is $r$-heavy, that is, $\abs{B_{r}(u)} > (d(1+\eps))^r$, then expand out the active vertices to include $u$ by growing a ball of radius $2 \cdot \ell_u$ around $v$. Set all vertices on the interior of the active set to be inactive. \item If no active vertices remain, this means that a new connected component of $H$ has been fully generated. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Explore components of $H$ by repeatedly growing balls around active vertices that reach $r$-heavy vertices.

nodes.name: Start a new component
nodes.statement: If there are no active vertices, select a vertex $v$ which has not been explored yet. If all vertices have been visited, terminate the process.
nodes.statement_short: Pick an unexplored vertex, or stop if all are visited.

nodes.name: Query neighborhoods of an active vertex
nodes.statement: Select a vertex $v$ in the active set, and iteratively query its radius-$r$ neighborhoods.
nodes.statement_short: Choose an active vertex and query its radius-$r$ neighborhoods.

nodes.name: Grow ball around heavy vertex
nodes.statement: If there is some vertex $u$ at distance at most $r$ which is $r$-heavy, that is, $\abs{B_{r}(u)} > (d(1+\eps))^r$, then expand out the active vertices to include $u$ by growing a ball of radius $2 \cdot \ell_u$ around $v$. Set all vertices on the interior of the active set to be inactive.
nodes.statement_short: If an $r$-heavy vertex is nearby, grow the active ball to include it and deactivate the interior.

nodes.name: Component completed
nodes.statement: If no active vertices remain, this means that a new connected component of $H$ has been fully generated.
nodes.statement_short: No active vertices means a component of $H$ is complete.

nodes.name: Poisson degree tails in sparse random graphs
nodes.statement: It is well known that for such a graph, the degree of any vertex $v$ has Poisson tails, in that for any $s \ge 1$, we have \[ \Pr[\deg{v} \ge sd] \le \exp(-\Omega(sd\log s)). \]
assumptions: for any $s \ge 1$

nodes.name: One-step distribution $P_x$
nodes.statement: Given a Markov chain $P$ on $\Omega$, and $x \in \Omega$, $P_x$ is the distribution over $\Omega$ obtained by taking one step of the Markov chain from $x$.

nodes.name: Spin flip $\sigma^{\oplus i}$
nodes.statement: Given $\sigma \in \{\pm 1\}^n$, $\sigma^{\oplus i} \in \{\pm 1\}^n$ is defined as \[ \left(\sigma^{\oplus i}\right)_j = \begin{cases} \sigma_j, & j \ne i, \\ -\sigma_i, & j = i. \end{cases} \]

nodes.name: Operator norm notation
nodes.statement: Given a matrix $M$, we denote its operator norm by $\|M\| = \|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}$.

nodes.name: Entropy $\Ent_\mu[f]$
nodes.statement: Given a distribution $\mu$ over $\Omega$ and a function $f : \Omega \to \R_{> 0}$, \[ \Ent[f] = \Ent_{\mu}[f] \defeq \E_{\mu}[f \log f] - \E_{\mu}[f] \log \E_{\mu}[f]. \]

nodes.name: Covariance notation
nodes.statement: For a random variable $X$ over $\R^k$, we use $\Cov[X]$ to denote the covariance $\E[XX^\top] - \E[X]\E[X]^\top$. For a probability distribution $\mu$ over $\R^k$, we use $\Cov(\mu)$ to denote the covariance of the associated random variable with law $\mu$.

nodes.name: Tree-excess
nodes.statement: Given a connected graph $G = (V,E)$, its \emph{tree-excess} is $|E|-|V|+1$.

nodes.name: Vertex and edge sets $V(H)$, $E(H)$
nodes.statement: Given a graph $H$, we use $V(H)$ and $E(H)$ to denote its vertex and edge sets respectively.

nodes.name: Non-isolated vertices $V'(H)$
nodes.statement: We use $V'(H)$ to refer to the subset of vertices of $V(H)$ adjacent to at least one other distinct vertex, the set of non-isolated vertices.

nodes.name: Principal restriction $M_S$
nodes.statement: For a matrix $M \in \R^{n \times n}$ and a set of vertices $S \subseteq [n]$, by $M_S$ we mean the $n \times n$ matrix where every row and column outside $S$ is zeroed out, i.e., the principal submatrix of $M$ restricted to $S$ but preserving the dimension.

nodes.name: Graph restriction $M_H$
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a graph on $[n]$, then by $M_H \in \R^{n \times n}$ we mean $M_{V'(H)}$, i.e., the restriction of $M$ to the non-isolated vertices of $H$.

nodes.name: Degenerate Gaussian $C^{-1/2}z$
nodes.statement: Given a matrix $C$ that is possibly not full-rank, and $\bz \sim \calN(0,I)$, we mean by $C^{-1/2} \bz$ the distribution supported on $\mathrm{Ker}(C)^\perp$ with density at $z$ proportional to $\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2} \cdot z^\top C z\right)$.

nodes.name: Glauber dynamics
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega = \{\pm 1\}^n$, and suppose that $\mu$ is supported on all of $\Omega$. The corresponding \emph{Glauber dynamics} Markov chain $P = P_\mu$ is described by the following transition law from any state $\sigma$: \begin{itemize} \item Choose index $i$ uniformly at random from $[n]$. \item Go to $\sigma^{\oplus i}$ with probability $\displaystyle\frac{\mu(\sigma^{\oplus i})}{\mu(\sigma)+\mu(\sigma^{\oplus i})}$, and stay at $\sigma$ otherwise. \end{itemize}
differentia: Choose index $i$ uniformly at random from $[n]$.
Go to $\sigma^{\oplus i}$ with probability $\displaystyle\frac{\mu(\sigma^{\oplus i})}{\mu(\sigma)+\mu(\sigma^{\oplus i})}$, and stay at $\sigma$ otherwise.
also_stated_at: Its evolution is described as follows: in each step, we select a uniformly random coordinate $i \in [n]$, and resample its assignment $\sigma_{i}$ conditioned on all remaining coordinates $\sigma_{-i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Glauber dynamics: pick a uniform coordinate and resample it from its conditional law.

nodes.name: Glauber dynamics is ergodic and reversible
nodes.statement: The Markov chain $P_\mu$ is ergodic and time-reversible (with respect to $\mu$), so has $\mu$ as its stationary distribution.
conclusions: The Markov chain $P_\mu$ is ergodic and time-reversible (with respect to $\mu$), so has $\mu$ as its stationary distribution.

nodes.name: Mixing time
nodes.statement:
Given a Markov chain $P$ with stationary distribution $\mu$, and a distribution $
u$ that is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$, the associated mixing time initialized at $
u$ is defined by \[ 	mix(P,\eps;
u) = \min\left\{ t > 0 : d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P^t
u,\mu) < \eps ight\}. \] We define the \emph{mixing time} to be \[ 	mix(P,\eps) = \max_{x \in \Omega}	mix(P,\eps;\delta_x). \]

nodes.name: Dirichlet form
nodes.statement: Given a distribution $\mu$ over $\{\pm 1\}^n$, a time-reversible Markov chain $P$ with stationary distribution $\mu$, and functions $f,g : \{\pm 1\}^n \to \R$, the associated \emph{Dirichlet form} is defined as \[ \mathcal{E}(f,g) = \mathcal{E}_{P}(f,g) \defeq \underset{\substack{x \sim \mu \\ y \sim P_x}}{\E} \left[ (f(x) - f(y))(g(x) - g(y)) \right]. \]

nodes.name: Modified log-Sobolev inequality
nodes.statement: Given a time-reversible Markov chain $P$ on $\{\pm 1\}^n$ with stationary distribution $\mu$, $P$ is said to satisfy a \emph{modified log-Sobolev inequality} (MLSI) with constant $C$ (possibly depending on $n$) if for any function $f : \{\pm 1\}^n \to \R_{> 0}$, \[ \mathcal{E}(f,\log f) \ge C \Ent[f]. \] In particular, $\MLSI$ is the best (largest) such constant $C$.
nodes.statement_short: MLSI with constant $C$: $\mathcal{E}(f,\log f)\ge C\,\Ent[f]$ for all positive $f$; $\MLSI$ is the best constant.

nodes.name: MLSI implies mixing time bound
nodes.statement: Given a time-reversible Markov chain $P$ with stationary distribution $\mu$, if $P$ satisfies a modified log-Sobolev inequality with constant $\MLSI$, then \[ \tmix(P,\epsilon) \le \frac{1}{\MLSI}\left( \log \log \frac{1}{\mu_*} + \log \frac{1}{\epsilon} \right), \] where $\mu_* = \min_{x : \mu(x) > 0} \mu(x)$.
assumptions: Given a time-reversible Markov chain $P$ with stationary distribution $\mu$
if $P$ satisfies a modified log-Sobolev inequality with constant $\MLSI$
nodes.statement_short: Mixing time is at most $\MLSI^{-1}(\log\log(1/\mu_*)+\log(1/\epsilon))$.
nodes.label: fact:mixing-mlsi

nodes.name: MLSI tensorization for product measures
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a distribution on $\{\pm 1\}^n$, and $(C_i)_{i=1}^{k}$ a partition of $[n]$ such that there exist distributions $\mu^{(i)}$ on $\{\pm 1\}^{C_i}$ with $\mu = \bigotimes_{i=1}^{K} \mu^{(i)}$. For the Glauber dynamics Markov chain, if each $\mu^{(i)}$ satisfies an MLSI with constant $\rho^{(i)}$, then $\mu$ satisfies an MLSI with constant $\rho = \frac{1}{n} \min_{i} \rho^{(i)} |C_i|$.
assumptions: Let $\mu$ be a distribution on $\{\pm 1\}^n$, and $(C_i)_{i=1}^{k}$ a partition of $[n]$ such that there exist distributions $\mu^{(i)}$ on $\{\pm 1\}^{C_i}$ with $\mu = \bigotimes_{i=1}^{K} \mu^{(i)}$.
if each $\mu^{(i)}$ satisfies an MLSI with constant $\rho^{(i)}$
nodes.label: fact:mlsi-product

nodes.name: Holley-Stroock perturbation principle
assumptions: Let $\mu,\nu$ be two probability measures over $\{\pm1\}^{n}$, and suppose that for some $c > 1$ (possibly depending on $n$), $\frac{1}{c} \leq \frac{\nu(\sigma)}{\mu(\sigma)} \leq c$ uniformly over all $\sigma \in \{\pm1\}^{n}$.
conclusions: Glauber dynamics for $\nu$ has MLSI constant at least $\MLSI / c^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Densities within factor $c$ change MLSI by at most $c^2$ and variances by at most $c$.
nodes.label: lem:mlsi-bdd-density-relate

nodes.name: Variance of linear functionals via covariance
nodes.statement: For any distribution $\mu$ on $\R^n$ with finite second moment, and vector $v \in \R^n$, \[ v^\top \Cov(\mu) v = \Var[\langle v,x\rangle]. \] In particular, \[ \sup_{\substack{v \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1} \\ \supp(v) \subseteq S}} \Var_{x \sim \mu}[\angles{v, x}] = \norm{\Cov(\mu)_S}. \]
assumptions: For any distribution $\mu$ on $\R^n$ with finite second moment, and vector $v \in \R^n$
nodes.label: fact:var-cov

nodes.name: Ising model
nodes.statement: The \emph{Ising model} corresponding to $J$ and $h$ is the probability distribution $\mu_{J, h}$ on $\{\pm1\}^n$, where \[ \mu_{J, h}(\sigma) \propto \exp\parens*{\frac{1}{2}\sigma^\top J \sigma + \langle h,\sigma\rangle}. \] Its \emph{partition function} is \[ Z_{J, h} \coloneqq \sum_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^n} \exp\parens*{\frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\top} J\sigma + \angles*{h,\sigma}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Ising model $\mu_{J,h}(\sigma)\propto\exp(\frac12\sigma^\top J\sigma+\langle h,\sigma\rangle)$ with partition function $Z_{J,h}$.

nodes.name: Diagonal invariance of Ising models
nodes.statement: A simple observation we frequently make use of is that for any diagonal matrix $D$, $\mu_{J, h} = \mu_{J+D, h}$.
assumptions: for any diagonal matrix $D$
nodes.label: obs:diag-invariant

nodes.name: Hubbard--Stratonovich transform
nodes.statement:
For any positive semidefinite matrix $C$ in $\R^{n	imes n}$: \[ \mu_{J, h} = \E_{z\sim
u} \mu_{J-C, Cz+h} \] where $
u$ is a distribution over $\R^n$ with density \[ 
u(z) \propto \exp\parens*{- rac{1}{2}z^{	op} C z + \log Z_{J-C, Cz+h}}. \] Further, $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J, h}} \psdle \Cov(
u)$.
assumptions: For any positive semidefinite matrix $C$ in $\R^{n\times n}$
nodes.statement_short: An Ising model is a Gaussian-smoothed mixture of Ising models with interaction $J-C$ and tilted fields.
nodes.label: thm:HS

nodes.name: Proof of the Hubbard--Stratonovich transform
nodes.statement: Let $\bsigma\sim\mu_{J, h}$ and $\by\sim\calN(0,I)$ be independent, and define $\bz \coloneqq \bsigma + C^{-1/2} \by$. The joint probability density function $p$ of $(z,\sigma)$ satisfies: \begin{align*} p(z,\sigma) &\propto \exp\parens*{-\frac{1}{2}(z-\sigma)^{\top} C (z-\sigma) + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\top}J\sigma + \angles*{h,\sigma}} \\ &= \exp\parens*{ -\frac{1}{2} z^{\top} C z + \angles*{Cz,\sigma} + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\top} (J-C) \sigma + \angles*{h,\sigma} } \end{align*} This tells us: \begin{align*} \mu_{J,h}(\sigma) &\propto \int_{\R^n} p(z,\sigma) dz \\ &\propto \int_{\R^n} \exp\parens*{ -\frac{1}{2} z^{\top} C z + \angles*{Cz,\sigma} + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\top} (J-C) \sigma + \angles*{h,\sigma} } dz \\ &= \int_{\R^n} \mu_{J-C, Cz+h}(\sigma) \cdot \exp\parens*{ -\frac{1}{2}z^{\top}Cz + \log Z_{J-C, Cz+h} } dz, \end{align*} which completes the proof of the first part. The PSD inequality $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J, h}} \psdle \Cov(\nu)$ follows from writing $\Cov(\nu)$ as $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J, h}} + C^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $z=\sigma+C^{-1/2}y$, expand the joint density and integrate out $z$.

nodes.name: Introduce smoothed variable and joint density
nodes.statement: Let $\bsigma\sim\mu_{J, h}$ and $\by\sim\calN(0,I)$ be independent, and define $\bz \coloneqq \bsigma + C^{-1/2} \by$. The joint probability density function $p$ of $(z,\sigma)$ satisfies: \begin{align*} p(z,\sigma) &\propto \exp\parens*{-\frac{1}{2}(z-\sigma)^{\top} C (z-\sigma) + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\top}J\sigma + \angles*{h,\sigma}} \\ &= \exp\parens*{ -\frac{1}{2} z^{\top} C z + \angles*{Cz,\sigma} + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\top} (J-C) \sigma + \angles*{h,\sigma} } \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $z=\sigma+C^{-1/2}y$ and write the joint density.

nodes.name: Integrate out $z$
nodes.statement: This tells us: \begin{align*} \mu_{J,h}(\sigma) &\propto \int_{\R^n} p(z,\sigma) dz \\ &\propto \int_{\R^n} \exp\parens*{ -\frac{1}{2} z^{\top} C z + \angles*{Cz,\sigma} + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{\top} (J-C) \sigma + \angles*{h,\sigma} } dz \\ &= \int_{\R^n} \mu_{J-C, Cz+h}(\sigma) \cdot \exp\parens*{ -\frac{1}{2}z^{\top}Cz + \log Z_{J-C, Cz+h} } dz, \end{align*} which completes the proof of the first part.
nodes.statement_short: Marginalize to express $\mu_{J,h}$ as a mixture of $\mu_{J-C,Cz+h}$.

nodes.name: Covariance comparison
nodes.statement: The PSD inequality $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J, h}} \psdle \Cov(\nu)$ follows from writing $\Cov(\nu)$ as $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J, h}} + C^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Cov$(\nu)$ equals Cov$(\mu_{J,h})+C^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Brascamp--Lieb inequality
nodes.statement:
For any distribution with density $
u\propto\exp(-V)$ for some $V:\R^n	o\R$, if there is a matrix $\Gamma\psdg 0$ such that $
abla^2 V(z)\psdge\Gamma$ uniformly, then \( \Cov(
u) \psdle \Gamma^{-1}. \)
assumptions: For any distribution with density $\nu\propto\exp(-V)$ for some $V:\R^n\to\R$
if there is a matrix $\Gamma\psdg 0$ such that $\nabla^2 V(z)\psdge\Gamma$ uniformly
also_stated_at: Suppose $\nabla^2 \log f(y) \psdge \Gamma$ for all $y$, where $f$ is the density of $\bz$. Then, $\Cov[\bz]\psdle\Gamma^{-1}$.
nodes.label: thm:brascamp-lieb

nodes.name: Covariance bound for a sum of interaction matrices
nodes.statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be interaction matrices in $\R^{n\times n}$, with $M_1$ positive definite, and let $h$ be an external field in $\R^n$. Suppose for some positive definite matrix $\Gamma$, the following holds for all $z\in\R^n$: \[ M_1 - M_1\cdot \Cov\parens*{\mu_{M_2, M_1z + h}} \cdot M_1 \psdge \Gamma. \] Then $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{M_1+M_2, h}} \psdle \Gamma^{-1}$.
assumptions: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be interaction matrices in $\R^{n\times n}$, with $M_1$ positive definite, and let $h$ be an external field in $\R^n$.
Suppose for some positive definite matrix $\Gamma$, the following holds for all $z\in\R^n$: \[ M_1 - M_1\cdot \Cov\parens*{\mu_{M_2, M_1z + h}} \cdot M_1 \psdge \Gamma. \]
nodes.statement_short: If $M_1-M_1\Cov(\mu_{M_2,M_1z+h})M_1\succeq\Gamma$ for all $z$, then $\Cov(\mu_{M_1+M_2,h})\preceq\Gamma^{-1}$.
nodes.label: lem:interaction-sum-cov-bound

nodes.name: Proof of the sum covariance bound
nodes.statement:
First, observe that by applying \Cref{thm:HS} with $C = M_1$, we obtain $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{M_1+M_2, h}} \psdle \Cov(
u)$ where $
u(z)\propto\exp\parens*{- rac{1}{2}z^{	op}M_1z + \log Z_{M_2, M_1 z + h}}$. It then suffices to bound $\Cov(
u)$. Towards doing so, we show that $
u$ is log-concave, and then use the Brascamp--Lieb inequality (\Cref{thm:brascamp-lieb}). We can verify that: \[ -
abla^2\log
u(z) = M_1 - 
abla^2 \log Z_{M_2, M_1z + h} = M_1 - M_1\cdot \Cov\parens*{\mu_{M_2, M_1z+h}} \cdot M_1. \] By assumption, for any $z\in\R^n$, $-
abla^2\log
u(z) \psdge \Gamma\psdg 0$, which establishes that $
u$ is log-concave. Consequently, by \Cref{thm:brascamp-lieb} we get $\Cov(
u)\psdle\Gamma^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Hubbard--Stratonovich with $C=M_1$, show the mixing density is strongly log-concave, then Brascamp--Lieb.

nodes.name: Apply Hubbard--Stratonovich
nodes.statement: First, observe that by applying \Cref{thm:HS} with $C = M_1$, we obtain $\Cov\parens*{\mu_{M_1+M_2, h}} \psdle \Cov(\nu)$ where $\nu(z)\propto\exp\parens*{-\frac{1}{2}z^{\top}M_1z + \log Z_{M_2, M_1 z + h}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound Cov$(\mu_{M_1+M_2,h})$ by Cov$(\nu)$ via the HS transform with $C=M_1$.

nodes.name: Reduce to log-concavity
nodes.statement: It then suffices to bound $\Cov(\nu)$. Towards doing so, we show that $\nu$ is log-concave, and then use the Brascamp--Lieb inequality (\Cref{thm:brascamp-lieb}).
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to bound Cov$(\nu)$ by showing log-concavity and using Brascamp--Lieb.

nodes.name: Hessian computation
nodes.statement:
We can verify that: \[ -
abla^2\log
u(z) = M_1 - 
abla^2 \log Z_{M_2, M_1z + h} = M_1 - M_1\cdot \Cov\parens*{\mu_{M_2, M_1z+h}} \cdot M_1. \] By assumption, for any $z\in\R^n$, $-
abla^2\log
u(z) \psdge \Gamma\psdg 0$, which establishes that $
u$ is log-concave.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $-\nabla^2\log\nu$ and bound it below by $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Apply Brascamp--Lieb
nodes.statement: Consequently, by \Cref{thm:brascamp-lieb} we get $\Cov(\nu)\psdle\Gamma^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude Cov$(\nu)\preceq\Gamma^{-1}$.

nodes.name: PSD lower bound $L-LML$
nodes.statement: Let $L,M$ be symmetric matrices such that $\|M\| \le \alpha$ and $0 \psdl \eta_1 \psdle L \psdle \frac{1-\eta_2}{\alpha}$. Then, \[ L - LML \psdge \eta_1\eta_2. \]
assumptions: Let $L,M$ be symmetric matrices such that $\|M\| \le \alpha$ and $0 \psdl \eta_1 \psdle L \psdle \frac{1-\eta_2}{\alpha}$.
nodes.label: prop:prop-hs-trick

nodes.name: Stochastic localization for Ising models
nodes.statement: A \emph{stochastic localization scheme} is a stochastic process $\parens*{\mu_{t}}_{0\le t\le 1}$ on the space of Ising models that is parameterized by a (possibly time-varying) \emph{control matrix} $(C_t)_{0 \le t \le 1}$ and an \emph{initialization} $\mu_{J,h}$, described by the following stochastic differential equation. \begin{equation} \dif\parens*{\frac{\mu_{t}}{\mu_{J,h}}} = \frac{\mu_{t}}{\mu_{J,h}} \angles*{ x-\E_{\mu_{t}} x, C_t \cdot \dif B_t } \end{equation} where $(B_t)_{0\le t\le 1}$ is the standard Brownian motion in $n$ dimensions.
nodes.statement_short: A measure-valued process driven by an SDE with control matrix $C_t$, started at $\mu_{J,h}$.
nodes.label: def:stoc-loc

nodes.name: Stochastic localization SDE
nodes.statement: \dif\parens*{\frac{\mu_{t}}{\mu_{J,h}}} = \frac{\mu_{t}}{\mu_{J,h}} \angles*{ x-\E_{\mu_{t}} x, C_t \cdot \dif B_t }
nodes.label: eq:stoc-loc

nodes.name: Form of stochastic localization measures
nodes.statement: The distribution $\mu_t$ is the Ising model \( \mu_{J_t, h_t} \) where $J_t = J - \int_{0}^{t} C_s^2 \dif s$ and $h_t = \int_0^t C_s \cdot \dif B_s + C_s^2 \E_{\mu_s} [x] \cdot \dif s$. Further, $\mu_t$ is a martingale, in that for any set $A \subseteq \{\pm 1\}^n$, $\E[\mu_t(A)|\mu_s] = \mu_s(A)$ for $0\le s\le t\le 1$.
conclusions: The distribution $\mu_t$ is the Ising model \( \mu_{J_t, h_t} \)
nodes.statement_short: Stochastic localization measures are Ising models with $J_t=J-\int C_s^2$ and form a martingale.
nodes.label: fact:stoc-loc-form

nodes.name: Entropic stability along stochastic localization
nodes.statement: Consider a stochastic localization process $(\mu_t)_{t \ge 0}$ with respect to (possibly time-varying) control matrix $(C_t)_{t \ge 0}$, started at an Ising model $\mu_0 = \mu_{J,h}$. Suppose that for every $h'\in\R^n$ and $t \in [0,1]$, \[ \norm*{C_t \cdot \Cov\parens*{\mu_{J_t, h'}} \cdot C_t} \le \alpha_t. \] Then, for any positive-valued $\varphi$, \[ \E \left[\Ent_{\mu_{1}}[\varphi]\right] \ge \exp\parens*{-\int_{0}^{1} \alpha_t \dif t} \cdot \Ent_{\mu_{J,h}}[\varphi]. \]
assumptions: Consider a stochastic localization process $(\mu_t)_{t \ge 0}$ with respect to (possibly time-varying) control matrix $(C_t)_{t \ge 0}$, started at an Ising model $\mu_0 = \mu_{J,h}$.
Suppose that for every $h'\in\R^n$ and $t \in [0,1]$, \[ \norm*{C_t \cdot \Cov\parens*{\mu_{J_t, h'}} \cdot C_t} \le \alpha_t. \]
nodes.statement_short: Covariance bounds $\alpha_t$ along the path give entropy conservation with factor $e^{-\int\alpha_t}$.
nodes.label: lem:entropic-stability

nodes.name: Annealing: MLSI from entropy conservation and terminal MLSI
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be an interaction matrix and $h$ be an external field. Let $(\mu_t)_{0\le t\le 1}$ be a stochastic localization scheme initialized at $\mu_{J,h}$. Suppose that \begin{enumerate} \item We have the entropy conservation inequality \[ \frac{\E[\Ent_{\mu_1}[f]]}{\Ent_{\mu_{J,h}}[f]} \ge \eps \] for all $f : \Omega \to \R_+$. \item Almost surely, \[ \MLSI(P_{\mu_1}) \ge \delta. \] \end{enumerate} Then, $\mu_{J,h}$ has an MLSI coefficient at least $\eps\delta$.
assumptions: Let $J$ be an interaction matrix and $h$ be an external field.
Let $(\mu_t)_{0\le t\le 1}$ be a stochastic localization scheme initialized at $\mu_{J,h}$.
We have the entropy conservation inequality \[ \frac{\E[\Ent_{\mu_1}[f]]}{\Ent_{\mu_{J,h}}[f]} \ge \eps \] for all $f : \Omega \to \R_+$.
Almost surely, \[ \MLSI(P_{\mu_1}) \ge \delta. \]
conclusions: Then, $\mu_{J,h}$ has an MLSI coefficient at least $\eps\delta$.
nodes.label: thm:anneal

nodes.name: MLSI for a sum of interaction matrices
nodes.statement: Let $M_1,M_2$ be matrices in $\R^{n \times n}$ with $M_1$ positive semidefinite, and suppose that for every external field $h' \in \R^{n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$, \begin{enumerate} \item $\left\| M_1^{1/2} \cdot \Cov(\mu_{(1-t)M_1+M_2,h'}) \cdot M_1^{1/2} \right\| \le q$, and \item Glauber dynamics for $\mu_{M_2,h'}$ satisfies $\MLSI\parens*{\mu_{M_2,h'}} \ge \delta$, \end{enumerate} then, for any external field $h \in \R^{n}$, \[ \MLSI\parens*{\mu_{M_1+M_2,h}} \ge \delta \cdot e^{-q}. \]
assumptions: Let $M_1,M_2$ be matrices in $\R^{n \times n}$ with $M_1$ positive semidefinite
$\left\| M_1^{1/2} \cdot \Cov(\mu_{(1-t)M_1+M_2,h'}) \cdot M_1^{1/2} \right\| \le q$
Glauber dynamics for $\mu_{M_2,h'}$ satisfies $\MLSI\parens*{\mu_{M_2,h'}} \ge \delta$
nodes.statement_short: Covariance bound $q$ along the path and MLSI $\delta$ for $\mu_{M_2,\cdot}$ give MLSI $\delta e^{-q}$ for $\mu_{M_1+M_2,h}$.
nodes.label: thm:sum-MLSI

nodes.name: Proof of the sum MLSI theorem
nodes.statement: We will use \Cref{thm:anneal} by choosing the stochastic localization to be that with control matrix $M_1^{1/2}$. \noindent The desired statement follows once we verify that the following are true: \begin{enumerate} \item $\displaystyle\frac{\E \left[\Ent_{\mu_1}[f]\right]}{\Ent_{\mu_{J,h}}[f]} \ge e^{-q}$ for every $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\R_+$, and \item $\MLSI\parens*{\mu_1} \ge \delta$ almost surely. \end{enumerate} \Cref{item:entropy-con} follows from \Cref{lem:entropic-stability}, and \Cref{item:final-MLSI} is true by assumption, which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Run stochastic localization with control $M_1^{1/2}$ and combine entropic stability with the annealing theorem.

nodes.name: Choose localization and reduce
nodes.statement: We will use \Cref{thm:anneal} by choosing the stochastic localization to be that with control matrix $M_1^{1/2}$. \noindent The desired statement follows once we verify that the following are true:
nodes.statement_short: Use the annealing theorem with control matrix $M_1^{1/2}$; two conditions must be checked.

nodes.name: Condition (1): entropy conservation
nodes.statement: $\displaystyle\frac{\E \left[\Ent_{\mu_1}[f]\right]}{\Ent_{\mu_{J,h}}[f]} \ge e^{-q}$ for every $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\R_+$, and
nodes.statement_short: Entropy conservation with factor $e^{-q}$.

nodes.name: Condition (2): terminal MLSI
nodes.statement: $\MLSI\parens*{\mu_1} \ge \delta$ almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: MLSI $\ge\delta$ for the terminal measure.

nodes.name: Verify both conditions
nodes.statement: \Cref{item:entropy-con} follows from \Cref{lem:entropic-stability}, and \Cref{item:final-MLSI} is true by assumption, which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Entropic stability gives (1); (2) holds by assumption.

nodes.name: Weighted adjacency $A_c$ and degree $D_c$
nodes.statement: We will use $A_c$ to denote the adjacency matrix of $G$, weighted according to $c$, and $D_c$ as the weighted degree function where $D_c[i,i] = \sum_{j\ne i} A_c[i,j]$.

nodes.name: Nonbacktracking matrix
nodes.statement: The \emph{nonbacktracking matrix} $B_c$ is a $2m\times 2m$ matrix indexed by directed edges in $G$ where: \[ B_{c}[uv, xy] = \begin{cases} c(xy) &\text{ if }v=x\text{ and }u\ne y \\ 0 &\text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \] We will use $B_G$ to refer to the \emph{unweighted} nonbacktracking matrix, i.e., when $c(xy)$ is equal to $1$ for every edge in $G$.

nodes.name: Bethe Hessian
nodes.statement: The \emph{Bethe Hessian} is defined as: \( \BH_{c} \coloneqq D_{c\wh{c}} - A_{\wh{c}} + I \) where $\wh{c} = \frac{c}{1-c^2}$. When all the weights are equal to $t$, the Bethe Hessian can be written as: \[ \BH_G(t) \coloneqq \frac{(D_G-I)t^2 - At + I}{1-t^2}. \]
nodes.label: def:bethe-hessian

nodes.name: Bethe Hessian--nonbacktracking spectrum relation
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the spectral radius $\rho(B_G) \le \frac{1}{\alpha}$ if and only if $\BH_G(t)\psdg 0$ for all $t\in(-\alpha,\alpha)$.
assumptions: For any $\alpha\in(0,1)$
conclusions: the spectral radius $\rho(B_G) \le \frac{1}{\alpha}$ if and only if $\BH_G(t)\psdg 0$ for all $t\in(-\alpha,\alpha)$

nodes.name: Proof that the Bethe Hessian of a tree is positive definite
nodes.statement: A simple observation is that when $G$ is a tree, its nonbacktracking matrix is nilpotent, and hence its spectral radius is equal to $0$, which gives us the following consequence.
nodes.statement_short: Nonbacktracking matrix of a tree is nilpotent, so spectral radius 0; apply the Bethe Hessian relation.

nodes.name: Bethe Hessian of a tree is positive definite
nodes.statement: When $G$ is a tree, for all $t\in(-1,1)$, we have $\BH_G(t)\psdg 0$.
assumptions: When $G$ is a tree
for all $t\in(-1,1)$
nodes.label: cor:bethe-tree-psd

nodes.name: Nonbacktracking walk count matrix $A_G^{(s)}$
nodes.statement: We define $A_G^{(s)}$ as the $n\times n$ matrix where the $i,j$ entry contains the number of length-$s$ nonbacktracking walks between $i$ and $j$.

nodes.name: Inverse Bethe Hessian as nonbacktracking walk series
nodes.statement: $\displaystyle \BH_G(t)^{-1} = \sum_{s\ge 0} A_G^{(s)}t^s$.
nodes.label: fact:bethe-inverse

nodes.name: Centered adjacency matrix
nodes.statement: Consider the adjacency matrix centered after conditioning on $\bsigma$, i.e., the matrix $\ol{A}_{\bG} \coloneqq A_{\bG} - \E[A_{\bG}|\bsigma]$.

nodes.name: Weight function $\bc$ of the centered adjacency matrix
nodes.statement: Let $\bc$ be the weight function on the edges of the complete graph prescribed by $\ol{A}_{\bG}$.

nodes.name: Nonbacktracking spectral bound for centered SBM
nodes.statement: For $\eps > 0$: \[ |\lambda|_{\max}(B_{\bc}) \le (1+\eps)\cdot\sqrt{d} \] with probability $1-o_n(1)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Liu, Mohanty & Raghavendra (LMR22), Theorem 7.4; Bordenave, Lelarge & Massoulie (BLM15)
assumptions: For $\eps > 0$

nodes.name: Proof of PSD-ness of the weighted Bethe Hessian
nodes.statement: By an identical argument to the proof of \cite[Theorem 5.1]{FM17}, the following is true.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as Fan--Montanari Theorem 5.1, using the nonbacktracking spectral bound.

nodes.name: Weighted Bethe Hessian is PSD for centered SBM
nodes.statement: For any $t\in\parens*{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}}$, \( \BH_{{\bc}\cdot t} \psdge 0 \) with probability $1-o_n(1)$.
assumptions: For any $t\in\parens*{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}}$

nodes.name: Proof of Bethe Hessian bounds for the centered adjacency matrix
nodes.statement: Recalling that the centered adjacency matrix is given by $\ol{A}_{\bG} = A_{\bG} - \E A_{\bG} | \bsigma$, and using the fact that the entries of $\E A_{\bG}|\bsigma$ are of magnitude $O\parens*{\frac{d}{n}}$, and the fact that all degrees in $\bG$ are at most $O(\log n)$ with high probability, we get the following relationship.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the weighted Bethe Hessian, using that $\E A|\bsigma$ entries are $O(d/n)$ and degrees are $O(\log n)$.

nodes.name: Bethe Hessian bounds for the centered SBM adjacency matrix
nodes.statement: For any $t\in\parens*{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}}$, we get that with probability $1-o_n(1)$: \[ \parens*{D_{\bG}-I}t^2 - A_{\bG}t + \E[A_{\bG}|\bsigma] \cdot t(1-t^2) + I (1 + o(1)) \psdge 0. \] Further, by using the fact that $\norm*{\E[A_{\bG}|\bsigma}] \le d\cdot(1+o(1))$, we get: \[ \wt{\BH}_{\bG}(t) \coloneqq \parens*{D_{\bG}-I}t^2 - \ol{A}_{\bG} t + I \cdot\parens*{1 + d|t|^3 + o(1)} \psdge 0\mper \]
assumptions: For any $t\in\parens*{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}}$
nodes.label: cor:bethe-bounds

nodes.name: Spectral norm of the centered adjacency matrix on bounded-degree vertices
nodes.statement: Let $S\subseteq[n]$ such that the degree of every vertex in $S$ within $\bG$ is at most $(1+\eps)d$, and suppose that $\sqrt{d(1+\eps)} + \frac{1}{1+\eps} \le \sqrt{d}(1+\eps)$. Then \[ \norm*{\parens*{\ol{A}_{\bG}}_S} \le 2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps) \] with probability $1-o_n(1)$. Consequently, the spectral diameter of $\parens*{\ol{A}_{\bG}}_S$ is at most $4\sqrt{d}(1+\eps)$.
assumptions: Let $S\subseteq[n]$ such that the degree of every vertex in $S$ within $\bG$ is at most $(1+\eps)d$
suppose that $\sqrt{d(1+\eps)} + \frac{1}{1+\eps} \le \sqrt{d}(1+\eps)$
conclusions: Consequently, the spectral diameter of $\parens*{\ol{A}_{\bG}}_S$ is at most $4\sqrt{d}(1+\eps)$.
nodes.statement_short: Restricted to vertices of degree $\le(1+\eps)d$, the centered adjacency matrix has norm $\le2\sqrt d(1+\eps)$ whp.
nodes.label: lem:bulk-spectral-radius

nodes.name: Proof of the bulk spectral radius bound
nodes.statement: We shall use \Cref{cor:bethe-bounds}. Set $t = \frac{1}{(1+\eps)\sqrt{d}}$. Observing that any principal submatrix of the PSD matrix $\wt{\BH}_{\bG}(t) \psdge 0$ is also PSD, and $\|(D_G)_S\| \le d(1+\eps)$, we get that \begin{align*} \lambda_{\mathrm{max}}\left((\ol{A}_{\bG})_S\right) &\le \frac{1 + dt^3 - t^2 + d(1+\eps)t^2}{t} \\ &\le \sqrt{d}(1+\eps) + \frac{1}{1+\eps} + \sqrt{d(1+\eps)} \le 2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps). \end{align*} Doing the same for the matrix $\wt{\BH}_{\bG}(-t) \psdge 0$, \begin{align*} \lambda_{\mathrm{min}}\left((\ol{A}_{\bG})_S\right) &\ge \frac{1 + dt^3 - t^2 + d(1+\eps)t^2}{-t} \\ &\ge - \sqrt{d}(1+\eps) - \frac{1}{1+\eps} - \sqrt{d(1+\eps)} \ge -2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps). \qedhere \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Take principal submatrices of the PSD matrices $\wt\BH_{\bG}(\pm t)$ with $t=1/((1+\eps)\sqrt d)$.

nodes.name: Choose $t$
nodes.statement: We shall use \Cref{cor:bethe-bounds}. Set $t = \frac{1}{(1+\eps)\sqrt{d}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the Bethe Hessian bounds with $t=1/((1+\eps)\sqrt d)$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $\lambda_{\max}$
nodes.statement: Observing that any principal submatrix of the PSD matrix $\wt{\BH}_{\bG}(t) \psdge 0$ is also PSD, and $\|(D_G)_S\| \le d(1+\eps)$, we get that \begin{align*} \lambda_{\mathrm{max}}\left((\ol{A}_{\bG})_S\right) &\le \frac{1 + dt^3 - t^2 + d(1+\eps)t^2}{t} \\ &\le \sqrt{d}(1+\eps) + \frac{1}{1+\eps} + \sqrt{d(1+\eps)} \le 2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Principal submatrix of $\wt\BH(t)\succeq0$ bounds the top eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $\lambda_{\min}$
nodes.statement: Doing the same for the matrix $\wt{\BH}_{\bG}(-t) \psdge 0$, \begin{align*} \lambda_{\mathrm{min}}\left((\ol{A}_{\bG})_S\right) &\ge \frac{1 + dt^3 - t^2 + d(1+\eps)t^2}{-t} \\ &\ge - \sqrt{d}(1+\eps) - \frac{1}{1+\eps} - \sqrt{d(1+\eps)} \ge -2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps). \qedhere \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Same with $\wt\BH(-t)$ bounds the bottom eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Nonbacktracking spectral bound for randomly signed graphs
nodes.statement: Let $\bG\sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$ and let $\bc$ be a random assignment of $\pm1$-valued signs to the edges of $\bG$. Then, with probability $1-o_n(1)$, \[ |\lambda|_{\max}\parens*{B_{\bc}} \le (1+o_n(1))\cdot\sqrt{d}\mper \]
assumptions: Let $\bG\sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$ and let $\bc$ be a random assignment of $\pm1$-valued signs to the edges of $\bG$.

nodes.name: Proof of the signed bulk spectral bound
nodes.statement: An identical argument to the proof of \Cref{lem:bulk-spectral-radius} can be used to establish the following.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the bulk spectral radius argument with the signed nonbacktracking bound.

nodes.name: Spectral norm of signed adjacency on bounded-degree vertices
nodes.statement: Let $\bG\sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$ and let $\bc$ be a random assignment of $\pm1$-valued signs to the edges of $\bG$. With probability $1-o_n(1)$, the following holds. Let $S\subseteq[n]$ such that the degree of every vertex in $S$ within $\bG$ is at most $(1+\eps)d$. Then, \[ \norm*{A_{\bc}} \le 2\sqrt{d}(1+\eps). \]
assumptions: Let $\bG\sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$ and let $\bc$ be a random assignment of $\pm1$-valued signs to the edges of $\bG$.
Let $S\subseteq[n]$ such that the degree of every vertex in $S$ within $\bG$ is at most $(1+\eps)d$.
nodes.label: lem:bulk-specrad-signed

nodes.name: Comparison of the two bulk spectral bounds
nodes.statement: Notice that one difference between \Cref{lem:bulk-spectral-radius} and \Cref{lem:bulk-specrad-signed} is that the latter does not require a constraint on $d$ and $\eps$. This owes to the fact that in the former case there are nonzero entries both at the scale of $\Theta(1)$ and $\Theta(1/n)$ whereas all nonzero entries in the latter case are in $\{\pm1\}$.

nodes.name: MLSI for randomly signed sparse SBM Ising models
nodes.statement: Fix $d > 1$. Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a randomly signed graph $\bG \sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$. There exists a universal constant $\beta > 0$ such that with high probability over the draw of $\bG$, for any external field $h$, we have $\MLSI(\mu_{\beta A/\sqrt{d}, h}) \ge n^{-1 - o(1)}$.
assumptions: Fix $d > 1$.
Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a randomly signed graph $\bG \sim \SBM(n, d, \lambda)$.
conclusions: There exists a universal constant $\beta > 0$ such that with high probability over the draw of $\bG$, for any external field $h$, we have $\MLSI(\mu_{\beta A/\sqrt{d}, h}) \ge n^{-1 - o(1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Whp, Glauber dynamics for $\mu_{\beta A/\sqrt d,h}$ on a randomly signed sparse SBM has MLSI constant $n^{-1-o(1)}$.
nodes.label: thm:main-mixing

nodes.name: Near-forest
nodes.statement: We say a graph $H$ is a \emph{near-forest} if all its connected components have at most a single cycle. Equivalently, each component has tree-excess at most $1$.
differentia: all its connected components have at most a single cycle

nodes.name: $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom graph
nodes.statement: We say a graph $H$ is \emph{$(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom} with respect to $S \subseteq V(H)$ if it satisfies the following: \begin{enumerate} \item For any $r\ge 1$, and any vertex $u\in V(H)$, the size of the $r$-ball around $u$ is at most $D^{r-1}\cdot\Delta$. Note in particular that this implies that the maximum degree is at most $\Delta$. \item For any $r\ge 0$ and $u\in V(H)$, $\abs*{\braces*{v\in S: \dist(u,v)\le r}} \le D^r$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Balls of radius $r$ have size $\le D^{r-1}\Delta$ and contain at most $D^r$ vertices of $S$.
nodes.label: def:pseudorandom-graph

nodes.name: $(\Delta,D)$-decomposition
nodes.statement: For a graph $G$, let $B, H$ be subgraphs of $G$ with possibly overlapping sets of vertices, which we refer to as the \emph{bulk} and \emph{near-forest} components. We say that $(B, H)$ is a \emph{$(\Delta, D)$-decomposition} of $G$ if the following properties hold. \begin{enumerate} \item $E(G) = E(B) \sqcup E(H)$, i.e. the bulk and near-forest components partition the edges of $G$. \item Let $\partial H = V'(B) \cap V'(H)$ denote the vertex boundary of $H$, the vertices in $H$ incident to an edge in $E(B)$. Then $H$ is a $(\Delta, D)$-pseudorandom near-forest with respect to $\partial H$. \end{enumerate} If such a $(B, H)$ exists, we say that $G$ admits a $(\Delta, D)$-decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: An edge partition of $G$ into a bulk $B$ and a $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom near-forest $H$ w.r.t. its boundary.

nodes.name: Covariance bound for Ising models on pseudorandom near-forests
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom near-forest with respect to $S \subseteq V(H)$. For any Ising model with interactions $J$ supported on $E(H)$ with values in $\bracks*{-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}, \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}}$, along with an arbitrary external field $h$, we have \[ \norm*{\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J,h}}_S} \le \frac{e^{2\gamma/\sqrt{D}}}{(1-\gamma)^2}. \] Additionally, \[ \norm*{\Cov\parens*{\mu_{J,h}}} \le \frac{e^{2\gamma/\sqrt{D}}}{(1-\gamma)^2} \cdot \frac{\Delta}{D}. \]
assumptions: Let $H$ be a $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom near-forest with respect to $S \subseteq V(H)$.
For any Ising model with interactions $J$ supported on $E(H)$ with values in $\bracks*{-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}, \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}}}$, along with an arbitrary external field $h$
nodes.statement_short: Ising models on pseudorandom near-forests with interactions $\le\gamma/\sqrt D$ have $O(1)$ covariance on $S$ and $O(\Delta/D)$ overall.
nodes.label: lem:near-forest-cov

nodes.name: Entropy conservation covariance bound for near-forest decompositions
nodes.statement: Let $(B, H)$ be a $(\Delta, D)$-decomposition of $G$, and let $J_B, J_H \in \R^{n \times n}$ be interaction matrices whose off-diagonal entries are supported on $E(B)$ and $E(H)$, respectively. Suppose that there are constants $\eta, K \in (0, 1)$ such that $\eta I_B \psdle J_B \psdle K I_B$, and that all interactions in $J_H$ are in $\left[ - \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} , \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} \right]$ for some $\gamma \in [0, 1)$. Finally, suppose that \[ K \cdot \frac{e^{2\gamma/\sqrt{D}}}{(1-\gamma)^2} \le 1 - \delta \] for a positive constant $\delta > 0$. There exists a positive constant $C$ not depending on $\Delta$ such that for any $0 \le t \le 1$ and external field $h \in \R^{n}$, \[ \Cov(\mu_{(1-t)J_B + J_H,h}) \psdle C (I_B + \Delta I_{H \setminus \partial H}). \]
assumptions: Let $(B, H)$ be a $(\Delta, D)$-decomposition of $G$, and let $J_B, J_H \in \R^{n \times n}$ be interaction matrices whose off-diagonal entries are supported on $E(B)$ and $E(H)$, respectively.

Suppose that there are constants $\eta, K \in (0, 1)$ such that $\eta I_B \psdle J_B \psdle K I_B$, and that all interactions in $J_H$ are in $\left[ - \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} , \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} \right]$ for some $\gamma \in [0, 1)$.
conclusions: There exists a positive constant $C$ not depending on $\Delta$ such that for any $0 \le t \le 1$ and external field $h \in \R^{n}$, \[ \Cov(\mu_{(1-t)J_B + J_H,h}) \psdle C (I_B + \Delta I_{H \setminus \partial H}). \]
nodes.statement_short: Along the localization path, covariance is $\preceq C(I_B+\Delta I_{H\setminus\partial H})$ when $K e^{2\gamma/\sqrt D}/(1-\gamma)^2<1$.
nodes.label: thm:entropy-conservation

nodes.name: Spectral assumptions on $J_B$ are without loss of generality
nodes.statement: The assumptions on the spectrum of $J_B$ may look artificial, but they are in fact without loss of generality. Indeed, by \cref{obs:diag-invariant}, one can shift $J_B$ by a constant multiple of $I_B$ to ensure it is PSD lower bounded by $\eta$ when restricted to the bulk.

nodes.name: MLSI for Ising models on pseudorandom near-forests
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom near-forest, and $J \in \R^{n \times n}$ an interaction matrix supported on $H$ with all interactions in $\left[ - \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} , \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} \right]$ for some $\gamma \in [0,1)$. There is a constant $c$ (depending on $\gamma$) such that for any external field $h \in \R^{n}$, \[ \MLSI(\mu_{J,h}) \ge \frac{1}{ne^{c\Delta}} . \]
assumptions: Let $H$ be a $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom near-forest, and $J \in \R^{n \times n}$ an interaction matrix supported on $H$ with all interactions in $\left[ - \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} , \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{D}} \right]$ for some $\gamma \in [0,1)$.
conclusions: There is a constant $c$ (depending on $\gamma$) such that for any external field $h \in \R^{n}$, \[ \MLSI(\mu_{J,h}) \ge \frac{1}{ne^{c\Delta}} . \]
nodes.statement_short: Ising models on $(\Delta,D)$-pseudorandom near-forests with interactions $\le\gamma/\sqrt D$ have MLSI $\ge 1/(ne^{c\Delta})$.
nodes.label: thm:mlsi-bdd-growth-tree

nodes.name: Near-forest decomposition of sparse SBM graphs
nodes.statement: Let $\bG\sim\SBM(n, d, \lambda)$ for any $d\ge 1$. There exist universal constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that for any $\eps \ge C_1 \cdot \left( \frac{C_2 + \log d}{d} \right)^{1/3}$, with high probability over $\bG$, we can partition the edge set $E(\bG)$ as $E(\bG_1) \sqcup E(\bG_2)$ for graphs $\bG_1$ and $\bG_2$ on $[n]$ where: \begin{enumerate} \item The maximum degree of $\bG_1$ is at most $(1+\eps)d$. \item $\bG_2$ is a $\parens*{\Delta, D}$-pseudorandom near-forest with respect to $S\coloneqq V'(\bG_1)\cap V'(\bG_2)$ for $\Delta = o(\log n)$ and $D = (1+\eps)d$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $\bG\sim\SBM(n, d, \lambda)$ for any $d\ge 1$.
for any $\eps \ge C_1 \cdot \left( \frac{C_2 + \log d}{d} \right)^{1/3}$
conclusions: with high probability over $\bG$, we can partition the edge set $E(\bG)$ as $E(\bG_1) \sqcup E(\bG_2)$ for graphs $\bG_1$ and $\bG_2$ on $[n]$ where:
The maximum degree of $\bG_1$ is at most $(1+\eps)d$.
$\bG_2$ is a $\parens*{\Delta, D}$-pseudorandom near-forest with respect to $S\coloneqq V'(\bG_1)\cap V'(\bG_2)$ for $\Delta = o(\log n)$ and $D = (1+\eps)d$.
nodes.statement_short: Whp a sparse SBM graph splits into a bulk of max degree $(1+\eps)d$ and a $(o(\log n),(1+\eps)d)$-pseudorandom near-forest.
nodes.label: lem:random-graph-decomposition

nodes.name: Bulk and near-forest parts of the decomposition
nodes.statement: We will henceforth refer to $\bG_1$ as the \emph{bulk} part in the decomposition, and to $\bG_2$ as the \emph{near-forest} part of the decomposition.

nodes.name: Role of the degree and $\Delta$ bounds
nodes.statement: The bound on the maximum degree of $\bG_1$ is important for obtaining a bound on the spectral norm of the interaction matrix restricted to the edges in $\bG_1$. The bound on $\Delta$ of $o(\log n)$ is crucial to obtain a bound of $n^{1+o(1)}$ on the mixing time via \Cref{thm:mlsi-bdd-growth-tree}.

nodes.name: Proof of the MLSI for randomly signed sparse SBM Ising models
nodes.statement: Consider the bulk $\bG_1$ and near-forest $\bG_2$ guaranteed by \Cref{lem:random-graph-decomposition}, and let $J_B = \frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} A_{\bG_1}$ and $J_H = \frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} A_{\bG_2}$. We will verify the conditions of \Cref{thm:entropy-conservation} for some $\beta = \Omega(1)$. We want to verify that \begin{align} K \cdot \frac{e^{2\gamma/\sqrt{D}}}{(1-\gamma)^2} \le 1-\delta \end{align} Before we dive into the calculations, let us first observe that from \Cref{lem:random-graph-decomposition}, we have that $\bG_2$ is a $(o(\log n),d(1+\eps))$-pseudorandom near-forest. Thus, the interaction strengths on $J_H$ are in $\left[ -\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} , \frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} \right] = \left[ - \frac{\beta\sqrt{1+\eps}}{\sqrt{d(1+\eps)}} , \frac{\beta\sqrt{1+\eps}}{\sqrt{d(1+\eps)}} \right]$. We will thus check \eqref{eq:conservation-condition} for $\gamma = \beta\sqrt{1+\eps}$. We have \[ \frac{e^{2\gamma/\sqrt{D}}}{(1-\gamma)^2} = \frac{e^{2\beta/\sqrt{d}}}{(1-\beta\sqrt{1+\eps})^2}. \] Turning now to $K$, \Cref{lem:bulk-specrad-signed} furnishes the bound \[ -2\beta(1+\eps) I_B \psdle J_B \psdle 2\beta(1+\eps) I_B. \] For some ``small'' $\eta > 0$ that we fix later, we can define $\wt{J}_B = J_B + (\eta + 2\beta(1+\eps))I_B$ without changing the Ising model to ensure \[ \eta I_B \psdle \wt{J}_B \psdle \left(\eta + 4\beta(1+\eps)\right) I_B. \] Thus, we choose $K = \eta + 4\beta(1+\eps)$. Hence, the LHS of \eqref{eq:conservation-condition} is at most \begin{align*} K \cdot \frac{e^{2\beta/\sqrt{d}}}{(1-\beta\sqrt{1+\eps})^2} \le e^{2\beta/\sqrt{d}} \cdot \frac{\eta + 4\beta(1+\eps)}{(1-\beta(1+\eps))^2}. \end{align*} If we have \begin{align*} \beta < \min\left\{ 1 , \frac{1+2e^{2/\sqrt{d}} - \sqrt{4e^{4/\sqrt{d}} + 4e^{2/\sqrt{d}}}}{1+\eps} \right\} = (3-\sqrt{8})(1 - o_d(1)) \approx 0.17 \cdot (1-o_d(1)), \end{align*} sufficiently small constants $\eta$ and $\delta$ may be chosen so the above is less than $1-\delta$. Now, we can apply \Cref{thm:entropy-conservation} to show that \[ \Cov(\mu_{(1-t)J_B + J_H,h}) \psdle C (I_B + o(\log n) \cdot I_{H \setminus \partial H}), \] and in turn \[ \exp(-\norm{\wt{J}_B^{1/2} \cdot \Cov(\mu_{(1-t)J_B + J_H,h}) \cdot \wt{J}_B^{1/2}}) \ge \Omega(1). \] On the other hand, \Cref{thm:mlsi-bdd-growth-tree} shows that for any $h'$ we have \[ \MLSI(\mu_{J_H, h'}) \ge \frac{1}{n} \cdot e^{-o(\log n)} = n^{-1-o(1)}. \] Finally, applying \Cref{thm:sum-MLSI} with $M_1 = \wt{J}_B$ and $M_2 = J_H$ allows us to conclude that $\MLSI(\mu_{\beta A/\sqrt{d}, h}) \ge n^{-1 - o(1)}$.

nodes.name: Set up bulk and near-forest interactions
nodes.statement: Consider the bulk $\bG_1$ and near-forest $\bG_2$ guaranteed by \Cref{lem:random-graph-decomposition}, and let $J_B = \frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} A_{\bG_1}$ and $J_H = \frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} A_{\bG_2}$.

Thus, the interaction strengths on $J_H$ are in $\left[ -\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} , \frac{\beta}{\sqrt{d}} \right] = \left[ - \frac{\beta\sqrt{1+\eps}}{\sqrt{d(1+\eps)}} , \frac{\beta\sqrt{1+\eps}}{\sqrt{d(1+\eps)}} \right]$. We will thus check \eqref{eq:conservation-condition} for $\gamma = \beta\sqrt{1+\eps}$. We have \[ \frac{e^{2\gamma/\sqrt{D}}}{(1-\gamma)^2} = \frac{e^{2\beta/\sqrt{d}}}{(1-\beta\sqrt{1+\eps})^2}. \]
nodes.section: 4.2 Proving an MLSI for diluted spin glasses

nodes.name: Bound $K$ via the bulk spectrum
nodes.statement: Turning now to $K$, \Cref{lem:bulk-specrad-signed} furnishes the bound \[ -2\beta(1+\eps) I_B \psdle J_B \psdle 2\beta(1+\eps) I_B. \] For some ``small'' $\eta > 0$ that we fix later, we can define $\wt{J}_B = J_B + (\eta + 2\beta(1+\eps))I_B$ without changing the Ising model to ensure \[ \eta I_B \psdle \wt{J}_B \psdle \left(\eta + 4\beta(1+\eps)\right) I_B. \] Thus, we choose $K = \eta + 4\beta(1+\eps)$.
